To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) security objectives are frequently implied by functional requirements, and (2), security-relevant sentences can be automatically identified from natural language requirements artifacts.

(1) 46% of all the sentences in requirements documents are security-relevant, (2) 28% of all the security-relevant statements explicitly state the security requirement while 72% imply the security requirement, and (3) 79% of these implied security requirements can be identified by using a combination of machine learning and natural language processing.

we can identify 79% security objectives from security-relevant natural language sentences in requirements documents, and we can automatically generate security requirements from these security objectives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
automatically identifying security objectives and security-relevant sentences from natural language requirements artifacts.
identifying security requirements from the natural language artifacts and translating them to a more formal representation.
identifying security-relevant information in requirements specifications that can be used by security engineers to develop functional security requirements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our tool-assisted process can help requirements engineers in automatically identifying security-relevance of sentences in natural language artifacts, classifying them based on security objectives and providing context specific templates for translating the security-relevant statements into functional security requirements.
we can identify security-relevant sentences with 82% accuracy and classify them with 79% accuracy.

our approach can be used to identify security-relevant sentences from natural language requirements and provide context-specific templates to help translate them into functional security requirements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we can automatically identify security-relevant sentences from natural language requirements artifacts and provide security requirements templates to translate the identified security requirements into a functional form that can be used for security analysis.
we can identify security objectives from requirements artifacts, classify them into different security objectives and then use these objectives as a basis to generate security requirements.
we have developed an approach to help identify the security-relevant information from requirements specifications and translate them into a set of security requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
security requirements are often hidden in plain sight, and we can help developers identify them by using a tool-assisted, machine-learning based approach.
security-relevant sentences can be automatically identified in requirements documents, and security requirements can be generated using the templates.
security-relevant sentences can provide valuable information about security requirements.
